phase_note: Generated 2026-10-11/12 by the Phase 11 spec batch (wave 2, in parallel with chart-catalog) in auto-approve mode, from base 560f909 (chart-kit specified, not yet implemented). 20 requirements / 129 acceptance criteria; 16 design components (11 dashboards modules: problems, grammar, directive, snapshot, region, source, storage, kinds, engine, report, binding; plus the query session and index facade amendments, the CLI command and pass, the declaration/layout/contract amendment, and the skill/docs/records surface); 8 major / 28 leaf tasks, (P): 3.1-3.4, 4.1-4.3, 7.1, 7.2 (9), with a stated stream order (group 3 merges before 4.1/4.2 branch; 4.3 may start after 2.2; integration points 5.1 and 7.3). Research: four read-only Explore subagents surveyed the codebase in parallel (CLI wiring and count pins; query sandbox and index facade; ownership, layout, declarations and writers; docs, text pins and precedents), plus scratch probes under sandbox-exec (deny network, verified EPERM) with a fresh HOME against synthetic DuckDB files on the venv's duckdb 1.5.6: P1 named_parameters ('?' and '$1' report as '1'; literals and comments ignored), description and relation type spellings, excess/missing parameter errors, TIMESTAMPTZ fetch needs pytz; P2 PyYAML strict composition (resolver-free loader, node style, duplicate keys, tags, aliases); P3 params-path memory (5M rows: execute+fetchmany 0.006 s / 42 MB vs .sql(params=) 0.88 s / ~297 MB; 20M: ~930 MB) and empty-mapping binding (execute(sql, {}) indistinguishable from execute(sql)). Downgrade: duckdb 1.2.0 could not be probed (no network to install it); its description vocabulary is taken from the discovery viability record and pinned by a two-vocabulary type map, and tasks 2.1, 4.3 and 6.3 run their checks on 1.2.0 where the implementer's environment provides it. No WebSearch/WebFetch (network-free run). Step 3.5 task-graph review ran as an independent reviewer dispatched by the controller, three verdicts. Round 1: RETURN_TO_DESIGN on one gap: the design widened IndexConnection.execute's params to a Mapping and called freshness.athlete_drift its only params caller, which was false (the index writer binds positional $1 through execute at store.py:400/426/486/500/513/523-524, and tests monkeypatch the Sequence signature), so every index write and mypy would have broken; plus 16 draft findings (1 blocking: the run-date mutation survived both tests named for it). Design fix, controller ruling option (a): execute stays byte-for-byte (signature, .sql(params=) routing, callers, tests); a new IndexConnection.execute_named(sql, Mapping) streams through connection.execute + fetchmany and binds nothing for an empty mapping; statement_parameters added; the query session always reads through execute_named; analytics-index Amendment 1 states the positional materialisation hazard as out of scope (the controller fixes the roadmap wording and queues the residual); research records the false claim and its correction (commits 7635fe1, 15477d0). Round 2 (after the design return): NEEDS_FIXES, 0 blocking, design gap and all 16 round-1 findings verified resolved; its 7 items were applied without a third review because the skill bounds the loop at one re-review: 2.1's streaming pin opens a file via create_index (the facade has no in-memory open) and asserts RSS growth (peak minus post-connect baseline, platform-normalised) under 100 MB instead of an absolute bound; a 1.2.0 floor clause for the streaming pin; an explicit (P) stream order across groups 3 and 4; a session-level test that run(params={}) reaches execute_named; IndexResult.from_cursor keeps the positional constructor (test_store_facade.py:119) unedited; two prose claims corrected (7.3 uses 7.1's live kind_names() check; 8.3's hash-seed mutation wording). Accepted trade-off: design.md (1495 lines) exceeds the template's 1000-line advisory; it carries four upstream amendments, the snapshot and report formats, and per-component contracts that tasks consume. Settled for consumers: no kind list or count anywhere in dashboards; the docs kinds block (between <!-- dashboard-kinds:start/end -->) equals kinds_markdown(describe_kinds()) and is regenerated by whichever of dashboards and chart-catalog lands second (task 7.3); amendments analytics-index 1, analytics-query 1, wiki-contract 5, connectors 3; CONTRACT_VERSION main+1 at merge ('10' at 560f909); CLI 13 -> 14 commands; PACKAGED_SKILLS 3 -> 4. Chart-kit seam gap G1 (minor, reported, no chart-kit edit): escape_markdown and clean_text are not facade exports and are not revalidation triggers; dashboards imports them from kit.format in region.py only and pins the behaviour it relies on. Cross-spec review round 1 (2026-10-12) applied fixes 1-5: the skill and docs now carry chart-kit's missing-row and non-finite notes (Req 18.3 wording, design § Skill and Docs with a note-by-note carry list, tasks 7.1/7.2 section-scoped phrase pins and drop-the-paragraph mutations); design's connectors e2e case is ('dashboard', ['refresh']) over a staged page, matching task 6.5; only CHANGELOG and the kinds block are shared with chart-catalog (pyproject mypy files and structure.md are sequential with chart-kit); design § Kinds states why kinds.py keeps its own cell escaper; the file plan lists tests/dashboards/test_published.py. Task 8.2 also checks, rather than amends, chart-kit's units paragraph.
